text:
lena: FYI — customer acme-prod opened a support ticket: sudden 429s and timeouts hitting their Dedicated endpoint after yesterday's billing credit/plan update. They say it started right after we rotated their API key.
sofia: Can you paste the exact error they're seeing? 429s can be rate or quota. Any X-RateLimit headers?
lena: Copying their summary: "POST /v1/generate -> 429 Too Many Requests intermittently, plus long tail latency spikes (p95 ~ 2.4s -> 8s) when traffic bursts. No 401s. They saw a spike at 14:02 UTC and again at 14:15." They included raw headers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 1000
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1670000
x-reserved-pool-id: rp-xyz
x-dedicated-cap: 180 rps
```
ajay: That x-rate-limit-remaining: 0 + reserved-pool header suggests the request was hitting the reserved pool cap. If their burst exceeded the pool's smoothing window, token bucket would emit 429s. Did we recently change their reserved QPS?
lena: Customer says they increased commit in Billing portal yesterday (from 120 rps -> 180 rps) and we rotated keys at the same time. Billing-bot shows the plan change completed at 13:58 UTC.
billing-bot: plan_update: customer=acme-prod plan=dedicated-tier-3 old_qps=120 new_qps=180 effective=immediate invoice=INV-9981
sofia: Ok — possibilities: plan change applied but throttles not warmed (rate-smoothing window mismatch), or backend route still routing to older pool config (cache TTL). Also key rotation could have led to duplicate warmup behavior (clients re-auth and create concurrent warmup traffic spikes).
infra-oncall: I'll check control-plane propagation and reserved pool config. Sending the command to inspect pool config for rp-xyz:
```
redwoodctl pools get rp-xyz --env=prod --output=json
```
infra-oncall: Output snippet: 
```
{"id":"rp-xyz","qps":180,"burst_window_ms":1000,"smoothing_ms":5000,"allocated_instances":4,"backpressure_policy":"reject"}
```
ajay: Smoothing_ms=5000 means the token bucket refills over 5s. If client sends a sudden spike of concurrent warmup requests (many new connections after key rotation), short-term QPS can exceed qps and hit 'reject' policy. We can temporarily switch to 'queue' or increase burst window to absorb.
rachel: The customer is on a tight SLA and is very sensitive to 429s. They asked for repro steps we can share — want to confirm before we suggest mitigation.
sofia: Proposed mitigation sequence: 1) Confirm control plane actually has qps=180 for all nodes (inflight check). 2) Temporarily set backpressure_policy=queue for rp-xyz and increase burst_window_ms to 2000 for the next 10m. 3) Ask customer to ramp traffic with a smoothing pattern (exponential ramp over 30s) and avoid instant key rotation-driven reconnect storms. 4) We'll monitor logs and X-RateLimit headers.
ajay: I'll run an immediate change with a short maintenance window. Running: 
```
redwoodctl pools update rp-xyz --set backpressure_policy=queue --set burst_window_ms=2000 --apply --reason="support triage acme-prod"
```
ops-bot: change_request: user=ajay action=update pool=rp-xyz status=accepted run_id=chg-7742

infra-oncall: Change applied across control-plane at 14:24:21 UTC. Confirmed via GET that backpressure_policy=queue and burst_window_ms=2000 now.
sofia: Lena — can you ask the customer to retry and share one sample request id or a short curl? Recommend they warm using paced traffic: `for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & sleep 0.3; done`
lena: Sent to customer. They replied: after we applied the change the 429s dropped immediately; p95 back to 1.7s. They did a reconnect storm at rotate — multiple clients reconnected simultaneously which produced the burst.
rachel: Great. Next steps for permanent fix: 1) update onboarding docs to recommend exponential ramp & connector libraries to stagger reconnects on key rotation. 2) Make control-plane config propagation faster / or atomic so plan changes don't leave transient nodes at old qps. 3) Consider default backpressure policy for Dedicated to be 'queue' for first 2 minutes after plan change.
ajay: Agreed on the docs + safer defaults. Also propose an autopilot when key rotation is performed in Billing: we can schedule a short 'burst absorb' window where we temporarily increase burst_window_ms and queue behavior to avoid reconnect storm thrashing.
sofia: Logging note for the ticket: include the control-plane trace id `cp-7742` and change run_id `chg-7742`. Also attach sample rate-limit headers and the customer's sample curl output.
lena: I'm closing the external ticket as "mitigated, awaiting follow-ups" and creating an internal follow-up: we must track control-plane propagation delta (ticket INT-5522).
sofia: Assigning owners: ajay -> implement autopilot change (RFC, tests), infra-oncall -> measure propagation once this week, rachel -> update customer onboarding docs.
ajay: Will open RFC and link INT-5522. ETA next week for a proposal.
infra-oncall: I'll run a 2h job to simulate key rotation reconnect storms in staging and measure whether current default burst_window_ms=1000 is sufficient. Will post results.
sofia: Thanks everyone :thumbsup: — leaving notes in case log search needed: search for `x-reserved-pool-id: rp-xyz` between 2026-08-10T13:50 and 2026-08-10T15:00 UTC.
ops-bot: ticket_update: external_ticket=SUP-4421 status=mitigated internal_ticket=INT-5522 owner=ajay
sofia: Closing thread.
